description: M5 (Epic 5, RES-G Slice C): HU limped-pot flop thresholds + authored rationale. The RES-G §4b directions live in sizing_rules as DATA (small polar lead; mostly-check OOP; big limped-pot bets are over-repped by value; texture decides the edge from a score=0 no-baseline start) — the graders (backend/app/domain/postflop.py::grade_limped_lead / grade_limped_vs_lead) read every direction-shaping number from here, never hardcode it. All values are [DERIVED-ASSUMPTION] design targets per RES-G; EVs stay approximate (heuristic, no solver).

rationale_parts.lead: Nobody raised before the flop, so neither player has a range edge — the board itself decides who this flop favors.
points: When you do lead (bet first into the limped pot), bet small and polar: real strength plus some air.
Check the medium-strength hands, especially out of position — a big bet into a limped field only gets action from hands that beat you.

rationale_parts.lead: You completed the small blind, so you'll play the whole hand out of position with a capped range (no premium hands) against another capped range: mostly check.
points: When you lead, keep it small and polar — strong hands and some air.
Building a limped pot out of position with a medium hand is the classic way to lose a big pot with a small hand.

rationale_parts.lead: A limper who bets this flop is polarized within a capped range — they rarely have the true top of the deck, but a BIG bet in a limped pot usually means real strength.
points: Continue with made hands and draws getting a fair price; fold the air.
Tighten the marginal calls as the bet gets bigger — size tells the truth in limped pots.

rationale_parts.lead: When the big blind stabs at a limped flop, it's first-to-bet aggression, not a strong preflop range — defend accordingly.
points: Call with made hands and draws that are getting a price.
Respect large bets — in limped pots the big sizings are heavy with value — and fold marginal one-pair hands more as the bet grows.
